newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Death threats force top Colombian judge to flee.
newsitem.headline: Death threats force top Colombian judge to flee.

text.p: The head of Colombia's National Judicial Association (Asonal) has left the country because of death threats, local media reported on Tuesday.
Bogota's El Espectador newspaper said Antonio Suarez Nino left Colombia Monday, apparently after being granted political asylum in a European country.
Details were not immediately available, but El Espectador said state security officials had warned Suarez Nino, a Bogota circuit court judge, of death threats again him since late last year.

Asonal is a trade union representing judges, judicial officials and court workers across Colombia. It staged several crippling work stoppages in the late 1980s and early 1990s to protest against the killing of dozens of judges by hitmen employed by drug gangs.
According to El Espectador, a sister of Suarez Nino left Colombia late last year after receiving death threats stemming from her work with a local human rights group.
Spokesmen for Asonal could not be reached immediately for comment on the reports.
